text:
alex.w: Seeing a weird correctness blip during canary - some requests after a shard handoff returned stale completions.
mika.k: ugh. repro and logs?
alex.w: Pasted minimal log snippet below. Happens when we soft-evict a prefix while the handoff is racing in.
alex.w: ```
2026-03-19T20:12:03Z INFO prefix=usr:123 action=soft-evict token=ev123 lease=ls456
2026-03-19T20:12:03Z DEBUG shard=7 handoff=start to=shard-8
2026-03-19T20:12:03Z WARN prefix=usr:123 served_from=kv_cache residency=stale
2026-03-19T20:12:03Z ERROR request_id=abc123 mismatch=kv->backend
```
priya.s: stack shows we mark residency cleared before confirming handoff applied on target. read-after-write hole.
sam.t: Can you sketch the current handshake? I thought we required a lease transfer ack.
alex.w: We do for hard-evict. For soft-evict we set `residency.soft=false` and let target pick up; no ack to avoid blocking hotpath.
luis.r: That seems like the root cause — soft-evict is optimistic and opens a narrow race window. But hard acks add latency.
priya.s: Proposal: split the API between `evict_mark(prefix)` and `evict_confirm(prefix, epoch)` where confirm is only required for cross-shard handoff. Local tenant-only evicts can stay optimistic.
mika.k: How do we detect cross-shard reliably? Current router may already know target shard but not the exact timeline.
alex.w: Router knows target shard id. Idea: emit a short-lived `handoff_token` (uuid + epoch) when you start moving, include token with subsequent cache gets. Target waits for token reachability or a `confirm` before flipping residency.
sam.t: Alternative: use a versioned residency number per prefix. Every time residency changes bump epoch. Reads require epoch >= observed. On handoff the target increments epoch when it takes ownership and writes epoch to meta store; origin waits for a watch on meta store when doing soft-evict.
luis.r: Meta-store waits mean more RPCs. That increases tail latency for evict-heavy workloads (customer A has lots of dynamic prefixes).
priya.s: Tradeoff matrix: correctness vs latency vs extra memory/RPCs. We should keep the fast-path no-RPC for same-shard evicts, but require a confirm for cross-shard.
ops-bot: Deploy 2026-03-19T20:15:00Z: canary v3.4.7 -> runtime-pool-canary :rocket:
mika.k: For implementation I'd prefer a lightweight in-memory lease epoch paired with a soft confirmation window (100ms) backed by a meta-store watch for retries.
alex.w: Sketch of fallback: if a read sees `residency=soft` and `handoff_token` present, it revalidate by 1) checking local pending handoffs map, 2) if unknown, make async check to meta-store (fast path documents), and 3) if still unknown, fall back to requerying backend (incurs cost but preserves correctness).
sam.t: We should add metrics: prefix_miss_after_soft_evict, handoff_token_lifetime, soft_evict_revalidate_count. Also histograms for added RPCs.
luis.r: Also watch memory: maintaining pending handoffs map per shard could grow. Limit to N=10000 entries per shard and LRU eviction; add a gauge for map_size.
priya.s: Action items: 1) write short RFC for `evict_mark` + `evict_confirm` + handoff_token pattern (owner @priya.s) 2) prototype small in-memory handoff map with meta-store watch fallback (owner @alex.w) 3) add metrics and a canary plan that simulates hotkey handoffs (owner @mika.k)
alex.w: I'll add logs that include `handoff_token` and `epoch` to make postmortems easier.
mika.k: Can we also add a debug endpoint to dump pending handoffs on a node? ephemeral, gated by admin flag.
priya.s: yes, gated behind --debug-admin, no prod exposure.
sam.t: timeline: RFC this week, prototype next sprint, canary next month. if canary shows tail regression >10% we'll iterate.
luis.r: 👍 Also include CPU and GC curves in canary dashboard.
alex.w: Thanks everyone. I'll start RFC draft in #eng-runtime and ping reviewers.
mika.k: pinging @devops for canary load shape later.
ops-bot: Incident note: observed 8 spikes in prefix_miss_after_soft_evict during 20:12-20:17 window. Logged.
priya.s: good signal. we'll tie the metric to the canary test cases.
alex.w: end of thread, creating PR reference in RFC once drafted.
